title: SiteForge — Someone Forgot to Clean Up
objective: The site's source is only ever served as rendered pages. Find a leftover backup file that serves the raw source instead.

verifier.condition: A request for a backup-style filename derived from a real application file returns that file's raw, unrendered source.

weakness: A static file server exposes an entire directory verbatim, including editor/deployment backup files left alongside the real source, which are served as plain text instead of being excluded or executed.
vulnerableEndpoint: GET /static/<name> (serves anything present in the directory, including backup-style files)
seededData: A simulated static directory containing the rendered site plus one leftover backup file a deploy script forgot to clean up.
hints: Browse the site normally first. Everything you see is rendered output, never raw source.
Editors and deploy scripts often leave a copy behind with a predictable suffix appended to the original filename — a tilde, '.bak', '.orig', '.swp'.
Guess at a backup-style name for a page you already know exists, like the homepage's source file.
burpNotes: Try common backup suffixes appended to known filenames directly under /static/ — no special tooling needed, just request candidate paths.
